lead.question:
let e := fun (t : ZMod 68) => ZMod.stdAddChar t
  let q := fun (i j : ZMod 68) => e (i^2 - i*j + j^2)
  let u : ℝ := (67 + Real.sqrt 4485) / 2
  ∃ (F : ZMod 68 → ZMod 68 → ℂ) (τ : ℂ →+* ℂ),
  F 0 0 = ((Real.sqrt u : ℂ) ^ 3) ∧
  (∀ i j, (i, j) ≠ (0, 0) → F i j * F (-i) (-j) = (q i j)⁻¹) ∧
  (∀ r s, (68 : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, ∑ j, F i j * F (r-i) (s-j) * q i j * e (-i*r+j*(r-s)) =
      (Real.sqrt 65 : ℂ) * F r s + if (r,s) = (0,0) then 68 else 0) ∧
  (∀ i j, (i,j) ≠ (0,0) → ‖τ (F i j)‖ = 1)

-- The finite algebraic conversion from these values to a rank-one Weyl fiducial.
lead.title: Open Quantum Problem 23: SIC-POVMs — hasSICPOVM 68 · step 1

review.statement: For fixed dimension 68, the supplied Left to Solve statement asks for a single function F : ZMod 68 → ZMod 68 → ℂ and a single unital ring endomorphism τ : ℂ →+* ℂ. The zero coefficient must equal (√u)³. The inverse-product identity and the unit-norm condition on τ(F i j) must hold at every nonzero pair. The twisted convolution must hold at all 4,624 pairs, including zero. The upstream Formal Conjectures declaration is `OpenQuantumProblem23.hasSICPOVM_68 : HasSICPOVM 68` and the consulted main-branch source still contains `sorry`. The catalogue page and its `/agent.txt` were inaccessible, so I used the supplied statement and could not verify its live points, exact declaration wrapper, or catalogue PR status. The public PR search surfaced no closing proof and was incomplete. [Upstream Lean source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/main/FormalConjectures/OpenQuantumProblems/23.lean)
review.significance: The coefficient statement is equivalent to existence of an exact Weyl–Heisenberg SIC fiducial in dimension 68. Its orbit supplies 4,624 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/69, which suffices for the upstream declaration. IQOQI Problem 23 asks for existence in every finite dimension and also lists stronger covariance and symmetry variants. [IQOQI Problem 23](https://oqp.iqoqi.oeaw.ac.at/sic-povms-and-zauners-conjecture)
review.settlement_test: An exact unit vector with all 4,623 nontrivial Weyl squared overlaps equal to 1/69 settles the supplied statement via the coefficient construction below. A proof that every unit vector violates at least one of those equalities settles its negation. Certification of the catalogue result requires an independent kernel replay of the exact declaration with its pinned imports.
review.aliases: Dimension-68 SIC-POVM, Weyl–Heisenberg covariant SIC or WH-SIC, complex equiangular lines, and complex equiangular tight frame. For the algebraic route, search for ghost SIC, twisted convolution, unitary Galois conjugate, and Zauner’s conjecture.
review.attempt: Andrew J. Scott supplied dimension-68 numerical fiducials in his 2017 search, with 150-digit data. Appleby, Flammia, and Kopp gave the conditional projector construction in Theorem 1.46 of their 2025 preprint and supplied the twisted convolution in their 2026 follow-up, building on Radchenko and Wheeler’s finite quantum dilogarithm identities. The manuscript *Stark units for real quadratic fields and reciprocity laws*, dated 4 October 2026 and prepared by Radchenko and Wheeler, claims the remaining modulus-one conjugate in Proposition 7 and applies it to SIC existence in §9.2. It credits Imran Zaidi with an earlier claimed result covering even dimensions with both d−3 and d+1 nonsquare, which includes 68. The later Khodaiemehr preprint gives a conditional route. I did not independently establish the October manuscript’s reciprocity argument or identify an exact dimension-68 witness with a replayable proof. [Scott](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.03993) · [Conditional construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.03970v2) · [Twisted convolution](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.39192) · [4 October manuscript](https://www.danrad.net/papers/stark-reciprocity.pdf) · [Khodaiemehr](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01524)
review.proof_or_witness:
Candidate mathematical reduction. Write X for the cyclic shift, Z for the clock with eigenvalues e(t), and choose ζ²=e(1). Define W(i,j)=ζ^(i²+j²) X^i Z^j. The phase is periodic modulo 68 and W(i,j)W(k,l)=e(−ik+jk−jl)W(i+k,j+l). I checked the exponent identity modulo 136 on all 21,381,376 index tuples. The W are trace-orthogonal and W(p)W(−p)=q(p)I. Thus A=(1/68)ΣₚF(p)W(p) satisfies the target convolution exactly when A²=√65 A+I.

Set b=(√65+√69)/2. Then b²=u, the polynomial roots are b and b−√69, and b³=68b−√69. Given an exact fiducial v, put A=bI−√69 vv*, F(p)=tr(W(p)*A), and τ=id. Trace gives F(0)=b³. The Weyl overlap condition gives |F(p)|=1 away from zero. Hermiticity gives F(−p)=q(p)⁻¹ overline(F(p)), yielding the inverse-product identity. The polynomial supplies the convolution at every pair.

Conversely apply τ entrywise. The images of the Weyl phases are roots of unity and the new clock root is primitive. The inverse-product and unit-norm hypotheses give τ(F(−p))=τ(q(p))⁻¹ overline(τ(F(p))). The zero coefficient is real because τ sends the real square roots in b to signed real square roots. Hence τ(A) is Hermitian, and (τ(b)I−τ(A))/τ(√69) is a Hermitian idempotent of trace one. Its range gives a unit vector with squared overlaps 1/69 for every nonidentity Weyl operator, after relabeling the clock index. Calculations and the source route are preserved in the [isolated notebook](/private/var/folders/kp/0gn1clkj59g9nzk16977plmh0000gn/T/tmpmnowuohr/work/checks/left_to_solve/sic68-notebook.md). This is a mathematical draft, with no completed Lean file or kernel replay.
review.remaining_obligation: Prove the exact lemma `∃ v : ZMod 68 → ℂ, (∑ t, ‖v t‖ ^ 2) = 1 ∧ ∀ i j, (i,j) ≠ (0,0) → Complex.normSq (∑ t, star (v (t+i)) * e (j*t) * v t) = 1 / 69`. For the literature route, specialize to the principal form x²−67xy+y² of discriminant 4485 and verify Proposition 7 for the attached finite quantum dilogarithm values, including one common conjugation for all nonzero values. Then formalize the Weyl coefficient conversion against the catalogue’s exact declaration and replay it independently. The Lean toolchain was unavailable in the workspace.
